questions.answer: I think it is preferable do live in a private flatshare, room, or appartment. I had friends that did that, and if I would go again, I would do that too. But it is more expensive.

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: At Sorbonne the bureaucracy and office work is in a state similar to how it must have been in Denmark 30 years ago, when the computer had just become commonly available.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was all about filling out blankets and handing them in. Exchange students can choose from a very wide selection of courses, but there is very limited guiding in what would be interesting for the particular student.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus coordinator from the faculty was not inclined to help. The webpage is impossible to navigate. The email correspondance is bordering on rude.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I succeeded.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is very easy to stress about, so my advice is to somehow not stress.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Their bachelor level courses do not have have as high an academic level as at the university of Copenhagen. Emphasis is put on memorisation. Critical thinking and engagement with theory is not encouraged or facilitated. Student do not have the possibility to become active subjects during the classes. The teacher hold the truth, and it is about acquiring their truth. But for learning french, it worked very well.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: See above. Additionaly, they have some very specific forms of assignments for example, the dissertation, the commentaire composé and more. These assignments must follow very specific structures. This is different from the UCPH, where there is more freedom. For me, it was beneficial to learn their structures, even though it was difficult and in some courses little to no help was offered.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Is it not as including. The subjects are not put into relation with the currents affairs and state of the world nor the everyday life, that we find ourselves in. Rather, the teaching tends to have an historic scope.

questions.answer: Of those courses, I would recommend littérature francaise 19-20e siècles, because the teacher of the seminars was very good, and had a more modern teaching style. Also, it was very nice to read Proust in french.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just talk to them. They might seem aloof or distant, but when you talk to them, they are nice and open. I think the atmosphere in the classes I was in was less friendly than at the UCPH. The french students seem less friendly with eachother too.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
In Paris there is a different attitude towards personal space. The city is crowded or even congested. I lived in the cité universitaire, which was nice, but I shared a kitchen with 30-40 people (which is part of the reason why I would have prefered private housing). 
The metro is crammed especially during rush hours. You are literally rubbing shoulders with multiple people. 
In the classes at the Sorbonne, there was not always enough seats and some students had to sit on the floor, even during tests/exams. 
The french have different approach to being ill and there is an obligation to attend classes. Therefore people often show up ill. I have tried sitting next to someone who was blowing their nose continually for three hours. This happened several times. 
The Sorbonne bulding is very old and there is a lot of noise outside the building. Therefore the staff rarely want to open the windows, which means that the air in the classrooms is for the most part very bad. Some of the rooms are even filled with mold. I had to change a class because of mold.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The language.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Live privately if you can afford it. 
Choose courses at master level even if you are doing your bachelor, since they seem to be more interesting. 
If you want a more easy stay, consider taking some courses in english. I took all my courses in french, except a french language C1 course. It meant I had a lot of studying to do, but regarding learning their specific ways of structuring papers, the different courses supported eachother, since the forms of writing were similar between the courses.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
It is not necessary to attend the lectures to pass or even excel at the exams. Halfway during my stay, I started mainly attending the seminars and skipping many of the lectures. There are many more classes to attend than at the UCPH, and this gave me a bit more breathing space. 
Attendance is only obligatory for the seminars. Often the relation between the seminars and the lectures is very vague, and the teachers are not the same.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: There was one teacher who insisted on evaluating all students the same. Therefore all the exchange students did not pass the mid semester exam. For the end of semester exam I studied very intensely, and I got a top grade, which was so high that it made up for the points my first exam lacked. Therefore my average was high enough for me to pass the course. This was very satisfying, also so I do not have to take another course or write a paper to make up for it at th UCPH. Most exhange students did not pass the course. It was littératures européennes. I do not recommend taking that course, also since the teacher of the seminars is not very good and communicating.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: See above. The exams. The difficulty of corresponding with relevant faculty.
